title: Documentation
projectsBody: Only an administrator can create a project, from the Projects page. The name starts as Name and is selected, so typing replaces it. Start with a Customers table adds a People table with Name, Mail, and one sample row. Open a project and use the info icon beside members to edit its description. The star saves the project to favorites. Right-click a project to rename or delete it. In the members dialog, a member can be removed or suspended for that project, and the last administrator cannot.
tablesBody: A table is a grid of columns and rows. New table at the end of the tabs can start blank, with four sample columns and three rows, or from a CSV you upload. For a CSV, name the table, say whether the first row is the header, and every column is text. Drag a tab to change its order. A line shows the gap where it will land. Add a column with the + at the end of the header or between two headers, and choose the type before it is created. Drag a grip to reorder a column or a row. A line shows that gap too. Sort and filter from the column header; those choices stay with your account. Hovering a column title shows its data type. Select rows or columns to duplicate, color, or delete them. The bar at the bottom of the grid closes with X. Export writes the visible columns only, not row notes, so the same file can be imported again. Import into an open table adds any missing header as a text column and fills matching columns. The display control beside Views switches the grid to a read-only chart. It sums number and numeric formula columns, grouped by status, tag, text, mail, or URL. Dimension per row keeps each row separate when those values match. Bar and doughnut categories use a repeating color palette. A line uses the app color, and a second value uses a lighter or darker shade of it. Line, bar, and doughnut are available. That choice stays with your account, and a synced mirror keeps its own. The same control opens a timeline. Choose a date column and at least one other column as the item title. A range is a bar, a single date is a point, and a line marks today. Zoom runs from months down to days, and to hours when the column stores a time. Rows without a date are listed under the timeline, where the date can be set. Drag a bar to move it without changing its length. The left edge sets the start and the right edge sets the end. Each item has its own row, ordered by its start, and that order updates while you drag. The scroll wheel and a pinch zoom while the pointer is over the timeline. When the axis is wider than the area, it scrolls sideways. The cell is saved when you release. A synced mirror and a locked table stay read-only.
formulasIntro: Each formula cell keeps its own expression. There is no = in front. A result is a number, text, a boolean, or a list of those. The cell shows a number as a number, text as text, TRUE or FALSE, and a list joined with a comma. An empty cell is empty. Write numbers as 1 and 3.5, text in quotes, and booleans as TRUE and FALSE. + - * / % work on numbers. & and CONCAT join text. = and <> compare two numbers, two texts, or two booleans. > < >= <= compare two numbers or two texts. Mixing a number with text is #VALUE. Name a column, a cell, or a link in brackets. Older names such as Amount and People.Name still work. Text, long text, mail, and url are text. Number and currency are numbers. A checkbox is TRUE or FALSE. A date is YYYY-MM-DD and a datetime is an ISO text. Status, select, and radio are the label you see. Tags, multi-select, and people are lists of labels. A relation used as a value is the linked row's title. The row id is the id shown in the grid. Media is empty. Errors are #CYCLE, #REF, #VALUE, #DIV/0, #LIM, and #N/A.
formulasThisRow: That column on this row. [Qty] * [Price] multiplies two numbers on this row.
formulasCell: One cell. #15 is the row number in the grid, so the value is a number you can add. A space or a dot in the column name stays inside the brackets.
formulasLink: Price on the record this row's Customer link points at. One link is one number. Several links is a list, so use SUM([Customer -> Price]).
formulasColumn: Every row of that column. A bracket with only a table and a column is a list, so math rejects it until SUM, AVERAGE, MIN, MAX, or COUNT folds it.
formulasLookup: Finds a row by a matching value when there is no link. The first and third brackets are columns on the same table. The middle one is the value on this row.
lookupBody: LOOKUP([People -> Mail], [Email], [People -> Name]) searches People Mail for the Email on this row and returns the Name from the matching row. The first and third arguments are columns on the same table. The middle argument is the value to find.

functions.SUM: Adds the numbers in a column.
functions.AVERAGE: Average of the numbers. Empty cells are skipped.
functions.COUNT: How many numbers are in the column.
functions.COUNTA: How many cells are not empty.
functions.ROUND: Rounds to the given number of digits.
functions.IF: Returns the second argument when the condition is true, and the third when it is false. Either value may be a number, text, or a boolean. Omitting the third argument returns FALSE. IF(Amount > 100, "High", "Low").
functions.IFNOT: IF with the condition reversed. Either branch may be a number, text, or a boolean. IFNOT(Paid, "Open", "Done").
functions.IFS: Returns the value of the first true condition. The value may be a number, text, or a boolean. No match is #N/A. IFS(Amount > 100, "High", Amount > 0, "Low").
functions.FOR: Walks each value in a list. Inside the second argument, IT is the current number, text, or boolean. The result is a list of the same length. IT outside FOR is #VALUE. FOR(Amount, IF(IT > 100, "High", "Low")). SUM(FOR(Amount, IF(IT > 0, IT, 0))) folds the list back to a number.
functions.AND: True when every condition is true. The result is a boolean.
functions.OR: True when any condition is true. The result is a boolean.
functions.NOT: Reverses true and false. The result is a boolean.
functions.ISBLANK: True for an empty cell, an empty list, or "".
functions.CONTAINS: True when text contains the part, or when a list of tags, people, or multi-select labels contains that label. CONTAINS(Tags, "Lead").
functions.COUNTIF: Counts rows whose column equals the condition. A text column stays text. COUNTIF(Status, "Open").
functions.SUMIF: Adds the number column on rows whose column equals the condition. SUMIF(Status, "Open", Amount).
functions.YEAR: The year of a date or datetime, as a number. YEAR(Date).
functions.MONTH: The month of a date or datetime, as a number. MONTH(Date).
functions.DAY: The day of a date or datetime, as a number. DAY(Date).
functions.LEFT: The first characters of a text.
functions.RIGHT: The last characters of a text.
functions.LEN: How many characters are in a text.
functions.LOOKUP: Finds the first row whose match column equals the value, and returns the result column. No match is #N/A. A table you cannot view is #REF. LOOKUP([People -> Mail], [Email], [People -> Name]).
functions.RELATION: Follows this row's link and reads a field on the linked record. Write [Customer -> Price]. Several links return a list, so SUM still works. An empty link is empty. A target you cannot view is #REF.
